content: Pride does not wish to owe, and vanity does not wish to pay.
author: François de La Rochefoucauld
sourceWork: Memoirs of the Regency of Anne of Austria
story:
There is a sharp, grounded clarity in this observation. Thinking about doing something gives us a comfortable dopamine hit of progress without any of the actual friction. We often use over-researching and planning as socially acceptable disguises for fear of starting.

François de La Rochefoucauld understood that real peace is never won by escaping the world or blaming external circumstances. Clarity follows action; it does not precede it. You cannot think your way into a new way of living—you have to act your way into a new way of understanding. The smallest real-world step beats the most brilliant theory.
reflectionPrompt: How can acknowledging your vulnerability help you build deeper self-trust and inner peace?
